tasks.short: Develop time and cost networks to plan large projects.

steps.what: Build the time and cost network.
Review the critical path the network shows.
Report slippage on the large project.

tasks.design: Activities are listed by the analyst. The {PROJECT} tool builds the time and cost network from durations and dependencies, which is tested in the product before any custom code. The analyst reviews the critical path and sends a slippage note only after that review.
tasks.previous_blocker: Networks were drawn in a sheet, and progress was a separate mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Durations and dependencies can drive a network. A wrong dependency still needs a person.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst sees a critical path that is politically impossible.

ambition.what: The analyst decides each week whether slippage is real or a bad dependency.

tasks.altitude: Drawing the network shrinks. Path review stays. The analyst can hold a slippage note the path review does not support.

reach.task: Keep a dependency list that a schedule can calculate
reach.learn: Which dependencies they refuse to invent to make a date

evidence.claim: A project tool can calculate a network from durations and dependencies.
A report assistant can answer questions on a prepared semantic model, and can misread a model that was not prepared.

assumptions: Focal role is the operations research analyst. Boundary: from a project brief to a slippage note. Running the project is the lead's work.
Structured fields are activity, duration, dependency, cost and percent complete. The analyst and the project lead produce them. Fallback: an activity with no duration is left out of the network.
Test native {PROJECT} scheduling before custom code.
Upkeep of 4 hours per 100 baseline hours covers dependency rules and the note template.
unknowns: Whether the project lead will maintain percent complete in the same tool.
How large a project must be before a network is worth it.
research_questions: What share of slippage is a bad dependency rather than a real delay?
Who is allowed to change a duration after the network is baselined?

incremental.description: Maintain network templates and dependency checks

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low case: dependencies are unknown and the list is the whole task. High case: the network and the progress view are configured, and the analyst reviews the path. Dates are not invented to suit a deadline.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Break systems into components and examine mathematical relationships.

steps.what: Assign numerical values to each component.
Examine the mathematical relationships between components.
Record the relationships that were kept.

tasks.design: Breaking the system into components, and examining the relationships, stay with the analyst. Numerical values are assigned from measurements by a rule, not by a guess. The {DATA_PLATFORM} stores only relationships the analyst kept.
tasks.previous_blocker: The breakdown and the arithmetic were the same private sheet.
tasks.enabler_now: A value with a measurement can be assigned by a formula. The breakdown is a judgement.
tasks.still_hard: A relationship that is true in the numbers and false in the operation.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst drops a neat equation that the floor will not recognise.
tasks.altitude: Arithmetic shrinks when measurements exist. The breakdown and the relationships stay the analyst's.

reach.task: Store a measured value with its source, separate from an interpretation
reach.learn: How they keep a number from becoming a conclusion

evidence.claim: Assigning a measured value can be a formula. Choosing the components cannot.

assumptions: Focal role is the operations research analyst. Boundary: from a system description to a relationship record. Building a full simulation is out of scope.
Structured fields are component, value, unit, source and relationship. Measurements produce the value. Fallback: a component with no measurement has no number.
Test a {DATA_PLATFORM} table before custom code.
Upkeep of 2 hours per 100 baseline hours covers value formulas.
unknowns: Whether measurements already exist for the components.
How stable the system boundary is.
research_questions: What share of components have a measurement rather than an estimate?
How often is a relationship rejected after the values are assigned?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low case: the system boundary is unclear and the breakdown is most of the hour. High case: values assign themselves from measurements and the relationships stay manual.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Educate staff in the use of mathematical models.

steps.what: Prepare a lesson on the mathematical models.

loop.input: Model description and a worked example
loop.output: Lesson outline with the example's numbers
loop.check: Analyst checks every number against the worked example
loop.stop: One draft; a number not in the example is removed
loop.why_not_simpler: A lesson is speech plus a sheet, not a model card

steps.what: Educate staff in the use of the models, in the room.
Leave the worked example for later questions.

tasks.design: A lesson outline is drafted from the model and a worked example, and the analyst checks the numbers. Teaching staff stays in the room. The {LMS} page holds that same example, not a tutor that answers in the analyst's place.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each class was prepared from scratch, and the example was not left anywhere the staff could find it.
tasks.enabler_now: A worked example can be stored. Teaching someone to use the model cannot.
tasks.still_hard: A staff member whose question shows they would misuse the model.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst sees the misunderstanding in the room.

ambition.what: Staff who cannot attend the class still get the worked example the class used.

tasks.altitude: Classes stay. Preparation of the example shrinks. The analyst does not hand teaching to a chat.

reach.task: Teach a colleague to use a measure without handing them an unchecked answer
reach.learn: Which examples they insist on checking by hand first

evidence.claim: Method choice, interpretation and advice to management stay with the analyst.
Article 4 has required AI literacy of staff since February 2025.

assumptions: Focal role is the operations research analyst. Boundary: from a model and a worked example to a class and a stored example. Building a course catalogue is out of scope.
Structured fields are model name, example input and example output. The analyst produces the example. Fallback: a number the draft invents is removed.
Test the {LMS} page before custom code. Do not add a bot that answers staff questions as the analyst.
Upkeep of 2 hours per 100 baseline hours covers the example when the model changes. Literacy here means staff can read the example, not that a model teaches them.
unknowns: Whether an {LMS} is already used for internal classes.
Whether works-council consent is needed if completion of the class is scored for individuals. This design does not score individuals.
research_questions: What share of classes repeat the same model?
How often do staff ask a question the example does not cover?

incremental.description: Refresh the worked example when the model changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low case: each class is a new model and the room is the whole task. High case: the example is reused and only the teaching stays. Individual performance is not dashboarded.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop business procedures, including accounting and logistics systems.

steps.what: Study the current accounting or logistics procedure.

loop.check: Analyst checks each step against the text
loop.stop: One pass; a step not in the text is dropped
loop.why_not_simpler: Procedures are prose with local exceptions

steps.what: Draft the procedure text from the agreed steps.

loop.check: Analyst edits any step that was not agreed
loop.stop: One draft; an extra step is removed
loop.why_not_simpler: The text has to be readable by the team, not only a flow

steps.what: Walk the procedure with the team that will use it.
Publish the procedure the team walked through.

tasks.design: Current procedure text is extracted to steps and checked. The new procedure is developed by the analyst and walked through with the team. {DOCS} publishes only the version that was walked, after the analyst confirms it. Native document templates are tested first.
tasks.previous_blocker: Procedures were rewritten in full, and the published file could differ from the walk-through.
tasks.enabler_now: Agreed steps can fill a template. Designing the procedure cannot.
tasks.still_hard: A local exception the current text does not mention.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst hears the step the team will skip.

ambition.what: A published procedure page the night team can open without asking the analyst to repeat the walk-through.

tasks.altitude: Design and the walk-through stay. Rewriting from a blank page shrinks. The analyst can refuse to publish a step the team did not walk.

reach.task: Write an operating procedure that matches the system people actually run
reach.learn: How they stop a step that exists only on the page

evidence.claim: A procedure can be drafted from agreed steps. The design and the walk-through stay with a person.

assumptions: Focal role is the operations research analyst. Boundary: from the current procedure to a published page. Changing the accounting system itself is out of scope.
Structured fields are step, role, system and exception. The current text and the walk-through produce them. Fallback: a step that was not walked is not published.
Upkeep of 2.5 hours per 100 baseline hours covers the template when a system name changes.
unknowns: Whether procedures currently live in {DOCS} or in personal files.
Who owns the procedure after publication, the analyst or the process owner.
research_questions: What share of procedures are updates rather than new designs?
How often does the walk-through delete a step?

approvals.approved_version: procedure version walked with the team

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low case: the current text is wrong and the design is done in the walk-through. High case: agreed steps fill the page and the walk-through confirms them. Nothing is published that was not walked.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Path reviews, system breakdowns, classes and procedure design stay. Network calculation and example filing take less time. The analyst can hold a slippage note or a procedure that was not walked.
reach: Software developers do not invent a dependency to save a date
Systems engineers stop a step that exists only on the page
skills_to_grow: Separating a calculated path from a bad dependency
Publishing only a procedure the team walked
role.ambitious_version: The analyst spends the week on judgement about paths, components, classes and procedures, with the arithmetic and the blank page already handled.
